cases.title: Expired
cases.what: Signed correctly; exp was 400 s before the recording.
cases.attack: None: it is just old. A client that keeps using it sees 401.

cases.title: Not yet valid (clock skew)
cases.what: The issuer's clock runs 90 s fast: iat and nbf are in the verifier's future.
cases.attack: None: a clock problem. Leeway of a minute or two absorbs it.

naive.why: issuer key by kid: signature valid

cases.attack: Replay a token stolen from (or legitimately held for) one service at another.

naive.why: issuer key by kid: signature valid

cases.what: Valid, but it only grants messages:read.
cases.attack: None: authenticated but not allowed (403, insufficient_scope).

cases.title: An ID token, not an access token
cases.what: Same issuer, same key, aud happens to equal the API (a client and API sharing one identifier). typ is JWT, not at+jwt.
cases.attack: Cross-JWT confusion (RFC 8725 s2.8): a token meant for one purpose accepted for another. Only explicit typing catches it.

pinned.why: RS256 with the issuer's key: signature valid

naive.why: issuer key by kid: signature valid

cases.title: Payload edited, old signature kept
cases.what: Someone added admin to scope and kept the original signature.
cases.attack: Privilege escalation by editing claims. Any real signature check stops it.

naive.why: issuer key by kid: signature invalid

cases.title: alg "none"
cases.what: Unsigned: the header says no algorithm, the signature part is empty.
cases.attack: Forge any claims. Works on a verifier that lets the token choose its algorithm.

cve.what: jsonwebtoken (Node) <= 8.5.1 defaulted to accepting none when verify() was called without algorithms

pinned.why: kid None is not in the issuer's JWKS

naive.why: header said none: no signature check

cases.title: HS256 signed with the public key
cases.what: HMAC-signed, using the issuer's RSA public key (which anyone can download) as the HMAC secret.
cases.attack: Algorithm confusion: the verifier feeds its RSA public key to HMAC because the header said HS256.

cve.what: jsonwebtoken (Node) before 4.2.2 accepted HS-signed tokens where RS was expected

pinned.why: InvalidAlgorithmError: The specified alg value is not allowed

naive.why: HMAC with 'the key' for kid lab-1, which is the RSA public key: HMAC matches

cases.title: kid pointing at /dev/null
cases.what: kid is a path; the verifier reads the key from that file, which is empty, so the HMAC key is empty.
cases.attack: kid injection: make the server use a key you know (an empty file, a public file, or SQL in a key lookup).

pinned.why: kid '../../../../dev/null' is not in the issuer's JWKS

naive.why: key read from the file named by kid: HMAC matches

cases.title: jku pointing at the attacker's keys
cases.what: Signed by the attacker; the header tells the verifier where to fetch the matching public key.
cases.attack: Key substitution: a verifier that fetches keys from a URL inside the token trusts whoever wrote the token (RFC 8725 s3.10 and RFC 7515 s4.1.2).

pinned.why: kid 'atk-1' is not in the issuer's JWKS

naive.why: public key fetched from jku: signature valid

cases.title: HS256 with a weak shared secret
cases.what: A service that uses HS256 with a guessable secret.
cases.attack: Offline guessing: one captured token is enough to test billions of secrets (measured below).

pinned.why: kid None is not in the issuer's JWKS

naive.why: the service's own (weak) HMAC secret: HMAC matches

crack.note: single thread, Python's hmac module on this laptop; GPU crackers are several orders of magnitude faster
